result:
Born into a world of silence, I was the only child in a bustling family who prized music above all. My mother's violin was her confidante, her father's saxophone was his muse, and my silence was the antithesis of their bliss.

Days turned into years without a single sound escaping me. It was as if I lived in a vacuum, constantly absorbing the melodies and harmonies around me without contributing to the symphony. I learned to listen quietly, to soak in the notes, to capture the tunes that filled the air. It was my lifeline.

Then, one year into this silent existence, my life changed forever. It began with a simple invitation – a party for the deaf. At the time, I was clueless about such affairs, assuming them to be exclusive gatherings for the silent majority. But my parents, always generous with encouragement, urged me to step out and explore the world of sound.

As I stepped into the party, a whirlwind of laughter, music, and mingling filled my senses. The sound was deafening to my ears. I was enveloped by an orchestra I had never heard before, by conversations I couldn't understand and languages I couldn't decode. There was joy, music, and human connections borne out of differences. It was overwhelming, yet exhilarating.

I sought refuge in the music room, a haven for the hearing impaired as well as their loved ones. My mother, standing before her violin, an old companion now, shared stories of beauty and emotions through narration, music, and dance. She wept silently as she closed her eyes, not just to the unseen tears of sorrow but to the invisible barriers we stood with.

That night, a child invited by her parents to explore the world of sound was taught the beauty of silence – her silent space. We stood together, not by the echo of her weeping violin, but by the profound silence she wanted her child to understand. In that silence, my story began to change.

The realization came slowly, like the beams of sunlight on a frosty morning. Just like how a deaf person hears the story behind every laughter, we, who can hear, are fortunate to partake in the unseen symphonies of silent prayers, mournful melodies, and fleeting whispers. The tragedy of being able to hear is not the limitless volume of sound but the constant clamor of noise, continually drowning the whispers and silences that enliven our lives – the messages, the absences, the hearts' beats.

And then, aloud, the deafening silence turned into the sweetest melody – a melody of understanding. It had seeped inside, digging deep into the recesses of my consciousness. At that moment, I realized I didn't need a note, a sound, a song. I just needed to listen.

From a child born into silence to a heart accustomed to the melody of understanding, the world of sound opened to me. I began to recognize and savor the moments of silence, the spaces in between notes, the silences of others just as much as the sound. It was only then that I understood the value of that single silent child, living out her existence in the midst of the loudest family gatherings. Despite the deafening silence, she was the center of the universe in her mother's heart.

All we have to do is listen. And with the power of listening, we start to share a part of the world inside and outside us. And in this sharing, we find a part of our story.
